title: Sections of pullbacks form a presheaf on the small etale site
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a morphism of schemes $a:A\to B$ and a sheaf of $\mathcal O_B$-modules $\mathcal G$ let $a^*\mathcal G$ be its pullback [def-pc-module-pullback], let $a_*$ be the pushforward, $(a_*\mathcal M)(V)=\mathcal M(a^{-1}V)$ with $\mathcal O_B(V)$ acting through $a^\sharp_V$, and $\eta^a_{\mathcal G}:\mathcal G\to a_*a^*\mathcal G$ the unit of the adjunction $a^*\dashv a_*$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]; for $s\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal G)$ put $a^*s=\eta^a_{\mathcal G}(s)\in\Gamma(B,a_*a^*\mathcal G)=\Gamma(A,a^*\mathcal G)$. For composable morphisms $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to C$ one has $(b\circ a)_*=b_*\circ a_*$, so $a^*b^*\dashv b_*a_*=(b\circ a)_*$ is the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], with unit $b_*(\eta^a_{b^*\mathcal G})\circ\eta^b_{\mathcal G}$; let $c_{a,b}:a^*b^*\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(b\circ a)^*$ be the composition isomorphism of pullbacks (an isomorphism $P_{b\circ a}\cong P_aP_b$ as in [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]) normalized by the units: the unique natural transformation with
$$(b\circ a)_*(c_{a,b,\mathcal G})\circ b_*(\eta^a_{b^*\mathcal G})\circ\eta^b_{\mathcal G}=\eta^{b\circ a}_{\mathcal G}\quad\text{for all }\mathcal G,$$
which exists and is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation]. For objects $u:U\to X$ and $u':U'\to X$ of the small etale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] and an $X$-morphism $g:U'\to U$ (so $u'=u\circ g$) define
$$\rho_g:\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)\longrightarrow\Gamma(U',u'^*\mathcal F),\qquad \rho_g(s)=c_{g,u}\bigl(g^*s\bigr).$$
Then:
1. $\rho_g$ is a homomorphism of abelian groups, and $\rho_g(as)=g^\sharp(a)\,\rho_g(s)$ for $a\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$, $s\in\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$;
2. $\rho_{\mathrm{id}_U}=\mathrm{id}$;
3. for $X$-morphisms $h:U''\to U'$ and $g:U'\to U$ of $X_{\Et}$, $\rho_{g\circ h}=\rho_h\circ\rho_g$.

Hence $u\mapsto\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$, $g\mapsto\rho_g$, is a presheaf of abelian groups (a contravariant functor from $X_{\Et}$ to abelian groups).

proof.text: Sections of the unit. Let $a:A\to B$ be a morphism of schemes. Since $a^{-1}(B)=A$, $\Gamma(B,a_*\mathcal M)=\Gamma(A,\mathcal M)$ for every $\mathcal O_A$-module $\mathcal M$, with $b\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$ acting as $a^\sharp(b)=a^\sharp_B(b)\in\Gamma(A,\mathcal O_A)$ (definition of $a_*$ in [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]). The unit $\eta^a$ of $a^*\dashv a_*$ [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction] is a natural transformation of functors $\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_B)\to\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_B)$ whose components are $\mathcal O_B$-module maps. Taking global sections: (i) $s\mapsto a^*s=\eta^a_{\mathcal G}(s)$ is additive and $a^*(bs)=a^\sharp(b)\,a^*s$ for $b\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal O_B)$; (ii) for an $\mathcal O_B$-module map $\varphi:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ and $s\in\Gamma(B,\mathcal G)$, naturality $a_*a^*(\varphi)\circ\eta^a_{\mathcal G}=\eta^a_{\mathcal G'}\circ\varphi$ reads $(a^*\varphi)(a^*s)=a^*(\varphi(s))$, where $a^*\varphi$ is the functor $a^*$ of [def-pc-module-pullback] applied to $\varphi$.

proof.text:
The composition isomorphism on sections. Let $a:A\to B$, $b:B\to C$, $\mathcal G$ an $\mathcal O_C$-module and $s\in\Gamma(C,\mathcal G)$. Evaluate the defining equation of $c_{a,b}$ (statement; [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation], with the composite unit of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]) on global sections, using $\Gamma(C,(b\circ a)_*\mathcal M)=\Gamma(A,\mathcal M)$ and $\Gamma(C,b_*\mathcal N)=\Gamma(B,\mathcal N)$ (step 1): the right side sends $s$ to $(b\circ a)^*s$, the left side sends $s$ to $c_{a,b}\bigl(\eta^a_{b^*\mathcal G}(\eta^b_{\mathcal G}(s))\bigr)$. Hence
$$(\ast)\qquad c_{a,b}\bigl(a^*(b^*s)\bigr)=(b\circ a)^*s\quad\text{in }\Gamma(A,(b\circ a)^*\mathcal G).$$

proof.text: Clause 1. $\rho_g$ is the composite of $g^*:\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)\to\Gamma(U',g^*u^*\mathcal F)$ and of the map on global sections of the $\mathcal O_{U'}$-module isomorphism $c_{g,u,\mathcal F}:g^*u^*\mathcal F\to(u\circ g)^*\mathcal F=u'^*\mathcal F$. By step 1 (i) the first is additive with $g^*(as)=g^\sharp(a)\,g^*s$ for $a\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$; the second is $\Gamma(U',\mathcal O_{U'})$-linear. Hence $\rho_g$ is additive and $\rho_g(as)=c_{g,u}(g^\sharp(a)\,g^*s)=g^\sharp(a)\,\rho_g(s)$.

source.place: Tag 03DR, equation (35.8.1) (label equation-quasi-coherent-presheaf), whose functoriality the source takes for granted; argument written by an agent

proof.text: Clause 2. Put $a=\mathrm{id}_U$, $b=u$. The pushforward $\mathrm{id}_{U*}$ is the identity functor (definition in [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]: $\mathrm{id}^{-1}V=V$ and restriction of scalars along the identity), so $\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_{u^*\mathcal G}$ is a natural map $u^*\mathcal G\to\mathrm{id}^*u^*\mathcal G$ and $\lambda_{\mathcal G}=c_{\mathrm{id},u,\mathcal G}\circ\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_{u^*\mathcal G}$ is a natural transformation $u^*\to u^*$. Since $u\circ\mathrm{id}=u$, the defining equation of $c_{\mathrm{id},u}$ reads $u_*(\lambda_{\mathcal G})\circ\eta^u_{\mathcal G}=\eta^u_{\mathcal G}$, which the identity of $u^*$ also satisfies. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] (both adjunctions $u^*\dashv u_*$, $\delta=\mathrm{id}$), $\lambda=\mathrm{id}_{u^*}$. Applied to $\mathcal G=\mathcal F$ on global sections: $\rho_{\mathrm{id}_U}(s)=c_{\mathrm{id},u}(\eta^{\mathrm{id}}_{u^*\mathcal F}(s))=\lambda_{\mathcal F}(s)=s$.

source.place: Tag 03DR, equation (35.8.1) (label equation-quasi-coherent-presheaf), whose functoriality the source takes for granted; argument written by an agent

proof.text: Clause 3. Let $h:U''\to U'$, $g:U'\to U$, $u'=u\circ g$, $u''=u\circ g\circ h$, and $s\in\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$. (a) By naturality of the unit $\eta^h$ (step 1 (ii), with $\varphi=c_{g,u,\mathcal F}$ and the section $g^*s$): $h^*\bigl(c_{g,u}(g^*s)\bigr)=(h^*c_{g,u})(h^*g^*s)$, so $\rho_h(\rho_g(s))=\bigl(c_{h,u\circ g}\circ h^*c_{g,u}\bigr)_{\mathcal F}(h^*g^*s)$. (b) By $(\ast)$ of step 2 with $a=h$, $b=g$, the $\mathcal O_U$-module $u^*\mathcal F$ and the section $s$: $(g\circ h)^*s=c_{h,g,u^*\mathcal F}(h^*g^*s)$, so $\rho_{g\circ h}(s)=c_{g\circ h,u}((g\circ h)^*s)=\bigl(c_{g\circ h,u}\circ c_{h,g,u^*\mathcal F}\bigr)(h^*g^*s)$. (c) Apply [lem-sc-left-adjoint-composition-iso-associativity] with $\mathcal C_0=\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_X)$, $\mathcal C_1=\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_U)$, $\mathcal C_2=\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_{U'})$, $\mathcal C_3=\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O_{U''})$, $L_{01}=u^*$, $L_{12}=g^*$, $L_{23}=h^*$, $L_{02}=(u\circ g)^*$, $L_{13}=(g\circ h)^*$, $L_{03}=(u\circ g\circ h)^*$ with the adjunctions of [lem-pc-module-pullback-adjunction]; the hypothesis $R_{ki}=R_{ji}R_{kj}$ holds since pushforwards compose strictly (statement), and its $c_{ijk}$ are $c_{012}=c_{g,u}$, $c_{123}=c_{h,g}$, $c_{013}=c_{g\circ h,u}$, $c_{023}=c_{h,u\circ g}$ (same defining equations). It gives $c_{h,u\circ g}\circ h^*c_{g,u}=c_{g\circ h,u}\circ c_{h,g,u^*\mathcal F}$ as maps $h^*g^*u^*\mathcal F\to u''^*\mathcal F$. Comparing (a) and (b): $\rho_{g\circ h}(s)=\rho_h(\rho_g(s))$.

source.place: Tag 03DR, equation (35.8.1) (label equation-quasi-coherent-presheaf), whose functoriality the source takes for granted; argument written by an agent

proof.text: Conclusion. The assignment sends each object $u:U\to X$ of $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] to the abelian group $\Gamma(U,u^*\mathcal F)$ and each morphism $g$ to the homomorphism $\rho_g$ (clause 1), in the reverse direction; clauses 2 and 3 are the identity and composition laws of a contravariant functor $X_{\Et}\to\mathrm{Ab}$, i.e. a presheaf of abelian groups.
